concepts: Balanced stance with feet shoulder-width apart
Hands up for defense and grip fighting
common_mistakes: Reaching for grips without proper footwork
key_details: Keep knees slightly bent for mobility
Weight distributed evenly on balls of feet
Head up, eyes on opponent's chest
Ready to shoot or defend takedowns

learning.description: The starting position where both grapplers are standing and facing each other with no grips established. This is where all standing exchanges begin in BJJ.
key_concepts: Maintain athletic stance with balanced base
Keep hands ready for grip fighting
Control distance to prevent immediate attacks
Stay mobile and ready to move in any direction
entry_steps: Start match or return to feet from ground
maintenance_steps: Stay light on balls of feet
Keep hands between you and opponent
Circle and move to prevent predictable patterns
React to opponent's movement and grip attempts
learning.escape_overview: Not applicable - this is a neutral starting position
common_mistakes: Not protecting neck from collar grips
goals: Prevent opponent from establishing their grips

concepts: Use elbow as frame to create space
Pull down to break opponent's posture
common_mistakes: Standing square instead of creating angle
Gripping without elbow frame on opposite side
Reaching with straight arm instead of bent elbow
key_details: Hand on back of opponent's neck
Elbow bent, pulling down and toward you
Opposite arm frames against opponent's shoulder
Step to side to create angle

learning.description: A standing position where you control the back of your opponent's neck with one hand while framing with the other. Creates posture control and sets up takedowns or guard pulls.
key_concepts: Control opponent's head to control their body
Use opposite hand as frame to create space
Pull down to break opponent's posture and balance
entry_steps: From standing neutral, establish hand on back of opponent's neck
Place opposite hand on their shoulder or bicep as frame
Step to the side to create angle
Pull neck down while pushing frame to off-balance
maintenance_steps: Keep elbow bent and close to body
Apply constant downward pressure on neck
Frame with opposite arm to prevent them closing distance
learning.escape_overview: Opponent can swim arm inside, establish own collar tie, or create distance by hand fighting
common_mistakes: Pulling straight down without stepping to angle
Standing square in front of opponent
Straight-arming instead of keeping elbow bent
goals: Set up single leg or double leg takedown
Snap opponent down to front headlock

concepts: One arm over opponent's shoulder, one arm under their armpit
Keep hips close to control opponent
Use over hook to control posture
common_mistakes: Allowing too much space between hips
Standing upright instead of driving forward
Not securing the overhook deep enough
key_details: Overhook hand grips behind opponent's back
Underhook hand cups their lat or reaches for far hip
Head on overhook side for pressure
Drive forward with legs to create pressure

learning.description: A standing clinch position with one arm over the opponent's shoulder (overhook) and one arm under their armpit (underhook). Common in wrestling and BJJ for takedowns.
key_concepts: Keep hips close to prevent separation
entry_steps: Lock hands behind their back or grip their lat
maintenance_steps: Pull with overhook, lift with underhook
learning.escape_overview: Opponent can pummel for underhooks, create space with frames, or snap you down
common_mistakes: Shallow overhook that can be escaped
Locking hands too high on back
key_details: Head on either side for pressure

learning.description: A dominant standing clinch position where you have both arms under your opponent's armpits with hands locked behind their back. Highly advantageous for throws and takedowns.
key_concepts: Control both sides of opponent's body
Prevent opponent from getting their own underhooks
entry_steps: Pummel second arm inside for second underhook
Drive chest forward and pull back tight
learning.escape_overview: Opponent must create space and pummel for their own underhooks or frame and push away
common_mistakes: Locking hands too high on back
goals: Transition to body lock for trips

concepts: Control one side of opponent's body
common_mistakes: Not using opposite arm as frame
Allowing opponent to get double underhooks
key_details: Underhook hand reaches for far hip or back
Opposite hand frames on bicep or shoulder

learning.description: A standing clinch position with one arm under the opponent's armpit. Provides control on one side and sets up for advancement to double underhooks or takedowns.
key_concepts: Control one side of opponent's body
Use opposite arm as frame for distance
entry_steps: From standing, pummel arm inside opponent's arm
Reach for far hip or lock behind back
Frame opposite arm on their shoulder
learning.escape_overview: Opponent can whizzer (overhook) the underhook, pummel for their own underhook, or create distance

concepts: Control hips for throws and trips

learning.description: A standing position where both hands are locked around the opponent's waist. Dominant position for executing takedowns, throws, and trips.
key_concepts: Use for trips, throws, and mat returns
entry_steps: From double underhooks, slide hands lower
Lock hands around lower back or waist
Pull opponent tight to your chest
learning.escape_overview: Opponent must create space by hand fighting, posting, or hip escape

concepts: Level change to penetrate opponent's defense
Drive forward with legs for penetration
Secure leg or legs for takedown
common_mistakes: Telegraphing the shot with upper body movement
Leading with head down exposing guillotine
key_details: Head up or to side, never straight down

learning.description: The act of dropping your level and driving forward to attack your opponent's legs for a takedown. Includes single leg, double leg, and high crotch entries.
key_concepts: Change levels to get under opponent's hips
Drive through target, not just to it
entry_steps: From standing clinch or neutral position
Drop level by bending knees (not waist)
Step penetration foot between opponent's legs
learning.escape_overview: Opponent can sprawl, guillotine, or wizzer to defend
common_mistakes: Bending at waist instead of knees
Not committing fully to the shot
goals: Secure single leg or double leg

concepts: Maintain good posture to prevent sweeps and submissions
Create space to initiate guard break
common_mistakes: Posturing too high making balance vulnerable
Putting weight on knees instead of feet
key_details: Keep posture upright with straight back
Hands control opponent's hips or collar
Weight on balls of feet, not knees
Elbows tight to defend collar chokes

learning.description: Position where you are inside your opponent's closed guard. Your goal is to maintain posture, break the guard, and pass to a dominant position.
key_concepts: Posture is king - stay upright to prevent attacks
Control hips to limit opponent's movement
Break guard before attempting to pass
entry_steps: End up between opponent's legs after takedown or guard pull
Establish base with one knee up or both knees
Grip opponent's collar or pants to control
maintenance_steps: Keep back straight and head up
Hands control opponent's hips or gi
Weight distributed on feet, not knees
learning.escape_overview: Break the guard using standing or kneeling guard break, then pass
common_mistakes: Hunching forward exposing neck to chokes
Flat on knees with no mobility
Hands too high allowing hip control
goals: Pass to side control or mount

concepts: Maintain pressure and base to prevent sweeps
common_mistakes: Allowing opponent to control both sleeves
key_details: Control at least one leg or grip

learning.description: Position where opponent's guard is open and you are working to pass around or through their legs to achieve a dominant top position.
key_concepts: Control opponent's legs to limit mobility
Work to pass around or through legs
entry_steps: Break closed guard or start standing
Establish grips on opponent's legs or gi
learning.escape_overview: Complete guard pass to side control, mount, or knee on belly

Pressure into opponent to limit mobility

Prevent opponent from recovering full guard

Letting opponent go to knees (dog fight)
key_details: Crossface or underhook to control upper body
Knee slide or backstep to free leg
Prevent opponent's bottom leg from hooking

learning.description: Position where opponent has trapped one of your legs between theirs while you work to free it and complete the guard pass to side control or mount.
key_concepts: Control upper body to limit opponent's options
Prevent underhooks and recovery to full guard
entry_steps: Opponent catches your leg during guard pass
Begin working to free trapped leg
maintenance_steps: Work knee slide or backstep to extract leg
Prevent opponent from going to knees
learning.escape_overview: Complete pass by freeing leg to side control, mount, or knee on belly

goals: Pass to side control or mount

concepts: Pin opponent's shoulders and hips to mat
Control opponent's near arm and far hip
common_mistakes: Weight too high on opponent's chest
Giving space for opponent to escape
key_details: Control near arm with your arm or head
Hips low, sprawled away from opponent

learning.description: A dominant top position where you are perpendicular to your opponent, chest-to-chest, pinning them to the mat. One of the fundamental top control positions in BJJ.

Prevent space creation with tight connection

Drop chest pressure on their chest
Control near arm with your arm or head
maintenance_steps: Control near arm to prevent framing
learning.escape_overview: Opponent must create frames and space to shrimp and recover guard
common_mistakes: Weight too high allowing easy bridge

concepts: Balance on opponent's belly with knee
Control opponent's collar and far arm
Gateway position to mount or back
common_mistakes: Weight too much on knee causing imbalance
key_details: Far hand controls opponent's far arm

learning.description: A mobile top position where you place one knee on opponent's belly/chest while maintaining balance and control. Excellent for transitions and creating reactions.
key_concepts: Balance is key - distribute weight properly
Pressure creates defensive reactions to exploit
entry_steps: From side control, bring near knee to opponent's belly
Control far arm with far hand
maintenance_steps: Be ready to transition on opponent's escape
learning.escape_overview: Opponent will try to push knee away or shrimp - use these to transition
common_mistakes: Posted foot too close or too far
goals: Transition to mount or back when they escape

Weight distribution too far forward or back

Hands control opponent's arms or post for balance

learning.description: The most dominant position in BJJ where you sit on top of your opponent's torso, straddling them. Provides maximum control and numerous submission opportunities.

Grapevine legs or spread base for stability
Control opponent's arms to prevent escape

Plant knee tight to opponent's armpit
Bring second knee to opposite side
Sit up with hips tight to chest

learning.escape_overview: Opponent must bridge and roll or shrimp to create space
goals: Attack with Americana, cross collar choke, or armbar
Transition to technical mount or back
Force opponent to give up back

concepts: Seatbelt grip for upper body control

Weight too far back allowing escape
key_details: Seatbelt grip (one over shoulder, one under arm)

concepts: Control near arm and far hip
Don't let opponent come up to guard

Weight distribution causing opponent to roll
key_details: Control near arm with one hand
Control far hip with other hand

Use weight to prevent opponent standing
entry_steps: Control far hip to prevent rolling
maintenance_steps: Work for back control by inserting hooks
learning.escape_overview: Force opponent flat and take back, or force to side control
common_mistakes: Letting opponent sit back to guard
Poor base allowing opponent to roll
goals: Force opponent flat to side control
Attack with clock choke or crucifix

concepts: Control opponent's posture - break them down
Create angles for attacks and sweeps
Use legs to control distance and posture
Guard is an attacking position, not defensive
common_mistakes: Being flat on back with no angle
Not controlling opponent's sleeves or collar
Keeping guard closed when opponent stands
key_details: Pull opponent down with collar grips
Angle body to create attack opportunities
Squeeze knees to limit opponent's movement

learning.description: Fundamental guard position where your legs are wrapped around opponent's waist with ankles locked. Provides strong control and numerous attacking options.

learning.escape_overview: Sweep opponent or submit them; if passed, recover guard or escape
common_mistakes: Keeping guard closed when opponent stands
goals: Attack with triangle, armbar, or kimura

concepts: Manage distance with legs and feet
Control opponent's sleeves, collar, and posture
Create angles for sweeps and attacks
Keep opponent from passing to side
common_mistakes: Flat on back with no movement
Not keeping opponent at optimal distance
Weak grips allowing opponent to break free
key_details: Feet on opponent's hips or biceps
Hips mobile and ready to move

Mobility is key - hip movement essential
Create angles for sweeps and attacks
entry_steps: Opponent opens your closed guard or you open it
Establish strong sleeve and collar grips
Create distance and prepare to attack
learning.escape_overview: Sweep opponent to top or return to closed guard
goals: Execute scissor sweep or hip bump sweep
Return to closed guard when advantageous
Attack with submissions from open guard

Create frames to prevent flat position
Recover full guard or sweep to top

Keeping lockdown too long without sweeping
key_details: Get to side or create angles

Get to side not flat on back
Use lockdown or frames to control

Get to your side facing opponent

Work to recover full guard or sweep

goals: Recover to closed or open guard
Execute half guard sweep to top
Prevent being passed to side control

Protect your neck at all times
common_mistakes: Turning away and giving up back
Flat on back with no frames
key_details: Frame on opponent's neck and hip
Shrimp hips away to create space

Protect neck - don't give up back

Prepare to shrimp and recover guard

learning.escape_overview: Shrimp to create space, insert knee, recover to guard

concepts: Sit back to guard when opportunity arises
Don't stay static - move to escape or return to guard

key_details: Look for opportunity to sit to guard

Sit to guard as soon as possible

Use to sweep or take the back

Letting opponent step over the hook

Near hand can grip pants or ankle

Create X shape with your legs

Hook other leg on outside of thigh forming X

Get underhook on trapped leg side

key_details: Ride on opponent's side from turtle
Ready to take back or submit

learning.description: Advanced top position riding opponent's back from the side while controlling both arms. Often reached from berimbolo or turtle. Excellent control with numerous attack options.
maintenance_steps: Prepare for back take or submission
learning.escape_overview: Transition to back control or attack submissions

concepts: Rolling under opponent to take back

learning.description: Dynamic technique rolling under opponent from inverted position to take their back. Signature technique of modern sport BJJ. Requires flexibility, timing, and excellent technique.
learning.escape_overview: Complete roll to back control or crab ride

concepts: Counter to leg drag and pressure passing
key_details: Lean back nearly touching mat with back

learning.description: Advanced defensive position with extreme backward lean (like the Matrix movie). Temporarily avoids pressure passes and leg drags. Requires excellent back flexibility. Not a destination - transitional position only.
learning.escape_overview: Snap back up to recover guard position

common_mistakes: Not getting knee in correct position
key_details: Knee in middle of opponent's legs

learning.description: Pressure passing position with knee in middle controlling opponent's legs and hips. Popularized by Bernardo Faria. Systematic approach to passing various guards using pressure and control.
entry_steps: Get knee in middle of legs
learning.escape_overview: Systematically pass to side control
common_mistakes: Knee position too high or low

concepts: Smash opponent's legs to one side
common_mistakes: Letting legs escape to other side

learning.description: Heavy pressure passing technique smashing opponent's legs to one side while driving shoulder into chest. Overwhelming pressure-based pass. Very effective against flexible opponents.
learning.escape_overview: Complete pass to side control or mount

key_details: Drive through to back or pass

learning.description: Modern passing technique dragging opponent's leg across their body to create passing angle. Very effective against DLR and modern guards. Creates back take opportunities.
key_concepts: Gateway to back or side control
learning.escape_overview: Complete pass or take back
